scope: Proposition 5.3 (Compatibility of the normalized height families) of the manuscript “Uniqueness of tangent flows at the first singular time of embedded surface mean-curvature flow” (preprints/Tangent-flow-uniqueness-2026-09-24/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 355 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 19b2f77a4cbfb0d5), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 67. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix the common pa- rameter p on the inner parameter ball and the matched numbers Z, Z∗ on each adverse end. Choose the fixed constants in the preliminary and refined contraction balls before B. Then the following hold for large B. (1) At a fixed positive physical radius on the first height turn, the normalized height solution with derivative interpolated between the preliminary circular profile and gc belongs to the preliminary uniqueness ball of Theorem 4.7 and to a fixed refined ball. It is the preliminary normalized solution with those same path and exit data. (2) Let VL be either of the two normalized solutions on longer canonical paths with zero remainder derivative at its own exit, and let gL be its relative height. At a common shorter incoming height section let ψL = ∂s(gL − gc) be its actual remainder derivative, in the shorter scalar coordinate. The restriction (VL|short, λL) belongs to the augmented ball (5.38) for the shorter canonical exterior solve with datum ψL. It equals that shorter normalized solve. The linear interpolation between the two data ψ− and ψ+ gives an actual normalized family whose endpoints are exactly the two restrictions. All constants are uniform in the shorter size Y ∈ [Y0, cB]. The comparison retains the compact multiplier, and all members use the same Z, Z∗ and observation value. The non- adverse paths, exit sections, and outgoing derivative prescriptions are the common frozen ones specified before the height construction.
